extracted.intended_audience: conference organizers/program chairs, researchers studying peer review, and reviewers interested in calibration (NeurIPS community)
extracted.subtask_description: Analysis and practical methods for modelling, calibrating, and evaluating conference peer review (NeurIPS-style). Includes Bayesian Dirichlet analysis of decision outcomes, a reviewer calibration GP model, Monte Carlo simulations, and diagnostics for reviewing pipelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Posterior probabilities of decision outcomes (consistent accept / inconsistent / consistent reject)
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute the posterior over the three outcome categories using a Dirichlet posterior: p | k, alpha ~ Dir(alpha + k). The posterior mean per outcome is (alpha_i + k_i) / sum_j(alpha_j + k_j) and variance formula is provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Dirichlet posterior with chosen prior alpha (uninformative prior used in the note). Report means and variances (e.g. display as m[i] +/- 2*sqrt(v[i])). Compare to a random-committee baseline (e.g. random selection probabilities).

rubrics_metrics.name: Accept precision (AP)
rubrics_metrics.description: Accept precision computed from posterior samples as ap = 2*k[:,0] / (2*k[:,0] + k[:,1]) where k[:,0] is consistent accept and k[:,1] inconsistent decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sample from posterior (Monte Carlo from Dirichlet(alpha + k)) and compute mean and variance; include error bars (±2*std). Note the factor of 2 because inconsistent decisions are accounted for across both committees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reject precision (RP)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reject precision computed from posterior samples as rp = 2*k[:,2] / (k[:,1] + 2*k[:,2]) where k[:,2] is consistent reject and k[:,1] inconsistent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Estimate via Monte Carlo sampling from Dirichlet; report mean ±2*std. Compare to random-committee expectation (e.g. 3/4 for reject precision in random baseline).

rubrics_metrics.name: Agreed accept rate (agreed accept fraction)
rubrics_metrics.description: Agreed accept rate computed from samples as aa = k[:,0] / (k[:,0] + k[:,2]) (fraction of accepted-vs-rejected outcomes that are accepted consistently).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Estimate with Monte Carlo sampling; report mean ±2*std. Optionally compute medians and percentiles; histogram results to check symmetry of densities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of uninformative Dirichlet prior and sensitivity to prior
rubrics_metrics.description: The analysis uses an uninformative prior (alpha = ones) for the Dirichlet posterior, but acknowledges that different priors could reflect process knowledge (e.g. expectation of more rejects).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perform sensitivity analysis on prior choices if modeling process-specific structure; if modeling the decision process rather than just sampling uncertainty, incorporate additional information into the prior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monte Carlo estimation and histogram checks
rubrics_metrics.description: Use Monte Carlo sampling from the posterior distribution to estimate derived statistics (accept/reject precisions, agreed accept rate) and produce histograms to ensure error bars reflect underlying densities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Draw many samples (e.g. 10k), compute statistics for each sample, and produce histograms with lines for random-committee reference values; if densities are symmetric medians/percentiles will be similar to means.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer calibration model (y_ij = f_i + b_j + ε_ij)
rubrics_metrics.description: Model each review score as y_{i,j} = f_i + b_j + ε_{i,j}, where f_i is paper objective quality, b_j is reviewer offset, and ε_{i,j} is subjective noise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume f_i, b_j, and ε_{i,j} are random variables with specified normal priors to reduce parameter count; use this decomposition to estimate bias-corrected paper scores and reviewer biases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assume subjective noise ε_{i,j} ~ N(0, σ^2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Model reviewer-specific subjective residuals as independent normal noise with variance σ^2 to reduce parameter dimensionality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This reduces free parameters and leads to a Gaussian marginal model for stacked scores; σ^2 is a key hyperparameter to be estimated (or grid-searched).

rubrics_metrics.name: Assume paper qualities f_i ~ N(μ, α_f)
rubrics_metrics.description: Model underlying objective qualities as Normal with mean μ and variance α_f.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set μ to the mean of all scores (maximum-likelihood solution) and treat α_f as a scale parameter to be optimized (closed-form update provided).

rubrics_metrics.name: Assume reviewer offsets b_j ~ N(0, α_b)
rubrics_metrics.description: Model reviewer offsets as zero-mean Normal with variance α_b, reducing parameters and enabling pooling across reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reparameterize in terms of ratios hat{α}_b = α_b / α_f and hat{σ}^2 = σ^2 / α_f; explore these two ratios on a grid and optimize α_f for each choice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reparameterization and optimization strategy (optimize α_f, grid over ratios)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reparameterize covariance k(i,j;k,l) = α_f(δ_{i,k} + δ_{j,l} * hat{α}_b + δ_{i,k}δ_{j,l} * hat{σ}^2) so that α_f can be optimized directly and the remaining uncertainty is in two ratios.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For each grid point of hat{α}_b and hat{σ}^2 optimize α_f via α_f = (1/|y|) y^T hat{K}^{-1} y; evaluate likelihood on the grid to choose parameters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical model fitting using GPy (GP regression)
rubrics_metrics.description: Construct covariance matrices K_f (paper-linear kernel) and K_b (reviewer-linear kernel) and fit a GP regression model with GPy to find maximum likelihood parameter values (sum.K_f.variances, sum.K_b.variances, Gaussian_noise.variance).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use tokenized PaperID and Email to create X1 and X2 one-hot matrices, join them into X, build kernels, and call model.optimize(). Inspect model parameters and log-likelihood; you can also construct K explicitly without GPy and compute K^{-1}, logdet, etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compute bias-corrected paper scores and covariances
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute s (mean bias-corrected quality scores) and covs (posterior covariance of scores) using K_s = K_f + σ^2 I and standard GP posterior formulas: s = K_s * alpha + μ, covs = α_f * (K_s - K_s K^{-1} K_s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these to predict corrected scores for papers and to sample jointly from the posterior distribution of paper qualities for downstream Monte Carlo acceptance simulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monte Carlo simulation for acceptance probabilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Sample joint bias-adjusted scores from multivariate normal (mean s, cov covs) multiple times, rank sampled scores, accept top-N (e.g. top 420), and compute the empirical probability each paper is accepted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Run many samples (e.g. 1,000) to estimate AcceptProbability for each paper; use results to define grey-area papers and to compute expected number accepted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Define grey-area by probabilistic thresholds
rubrics_metrics.description: Define a 'grey area' of papers whose accept-probability lies between lower and upper thresholds (example lower = 0.1, upper = 0.9) representing papers debated most during teleconferences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Count number of papers in grey area and use this set to focus discussion between program chairs and area chairs; choose thresholds based on operational preferences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Laplace smoothing of accept probabilities before merging
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply a small smoothing adjustment to empirical accept probabilities (e.g. (prob_accept + 0.0002)/1.001) to avoid exact zeros or ones before joining with other data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prevents degenerate 0/1 probabilities in downstream analyses (e.g., joins, logs).

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanity checks and diagnostic plots
rubrics_metrics.description: Produce histograms and scatter plots such as calibrated reviewer scores histogram, raw score vs log-odds of accept, calibrated vs original scores scatter, and review bias histograms to validate model behavior.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use visual diagnostics to ensure no unexpected artifacts (e.g., check calibrated scores distribution, reviewer bias magnitudes). Save figures for reporting and sanity checking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compute reviewer bias posterior and export adjustments
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute posterior mean and standard deviation of reviewer offsets b and aggregate per-reviewer bias scores (ReviewerBiasMean and ReviewerBiasStd); optionally export to CMT-compatible CSV format for use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use K_b and covb formulas to compute b and covb; map back to reviewer emails and export. Include Impact Score and Confidence columns if required by downstream workflow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simulate conference with subjective/objective decomposition
rubrics_metrics.description: Simulate many papers with an objective score component and subjective reviewer noise component (e.g. subjectivity_portion=0.5) to study how accept rate and number of reviewers affect consistent acceptance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Vary number_of_reviewers and accept_rate, draw samples for objective and subjective parts, compute consistent_accept fraction across two independent committees; use large samples (e.g. 100k) for stable estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measure correlations for duplicate papers across committees
rubrics_metrics.description: For duplicate submissions evaluated by two independent committees, compute correlation coefficients for quality, calibrated quality, impact, and confidence (e.g., quality_cor = corrcoef(quality.T)[0,1]).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report correlation values and visualize with jittered scatter plots to understand inter-committee agreement and the effect of calibration on correlations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Track final fate of rejected papers (outlet mapping)
rubrics_metrics.description: Search for rejected papers (e.g., via Semantic Scholar) to determine later publication venues and produce Sankey diagrams showing flow from NeurIPS submission to eventual publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware of temporal/deadline biases (venues with deadlines soon after NeurIPS decisions will be overrepresented). Use mapping files to normalize outlet names and report counts per venue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correlation between quality/impact/confidence and long-term citations
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute bootstrap estimates of correlations between average_quality, average_impact, average_confidence and log10(1+citations) for accepted and rejected papers separately; add differential privacy noise to plots while computing correlations on raw data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bootstrap (e.g., 1000 resamples) to estimate mean correlation and ±2*std; separate accepted and rejected groups to avoid selection bias (conference acceptance may itself increase citations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish sensitivity analysis from full process modeling
rubrics_metrics.description: Be explicit whether the exercise is a sensitivity analysis (minimal modeling choices, e.g. uninformative priors) or a full model of decision-making (which should leverage more information about the process).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If modeling the full decision process, incorporate relevant structural information (e.g., accept rates, expected asymmetry between accepts/rejects, possible collusion) rather than relying solely on uninformative priors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compute log-likelihood and negative log-likelihood diagnostics
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute negative log-likelihood of the multivariate Gaussian model with covariance K and mean zero after removing data mean; use expressions involving logdet and quadratic form y^T K^{-1} y to evaluate model fit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these values to compare parameter choices on the grid; report numerical optimization outputs (e.g., GPy Objective and Parameters) to support reproducibility.
